title: [review] project-LICHEN-worker6-tkjl: write_to and from_bytes header bit layout incompatible with test vectors
description:
## Bug: Header bit layout mismatch vs shared test vectors

**File:** `rust/lichen-schc/src/fragment.rs:154,176-177,255,274,284`

**Severity:** P0 — spec compliance, interop failure

The shared test vectors (`test/vectors/schc_fragmentation.json`) use the following bit layout for Fragment headers:
- **Bit 7** (MSB): window bit
- **Bits 6..1**: FCN (6 bits, shifted left by 1 to leave bit 0 for first payload byte top bit)
- **Bit 0**: top bit of first data byte (ORed by the interleaved 7-bit encoding)

However, `write_to` and `from_bytes` use:
- **Bit 6** (`FRAGMENT_N`): window bit  
- **Bits 5..0**: FCN

This makes the wire format incompatible with canonical test vectors.

**Evidence:**
Test vector `tile_0` (FCN=62, window=0): expected wire header `0x7c`
- With FRAGMENT_N=6: `((window << 7) | (fcn << 1)) = ((0 << 7) | (62 << 1)) = 0x7c` ✓
- Our code: `out[1] = ((0 << 6) | 62) = 0x3e` ✗ (test fails)

The `fragmentation_vectors` test fails with assertion error comparing `[120, 62, ...]` (our output) vs `[120, 124, ...]` (test vector expected `0x7c = 124`).

**Fix approach:**
- `write_to`: `out[1] = ((window & 1) << 7) | ((fcn & 63) << 1);`
- `from_bytes`: `window = (data[1] >> 7) & 1; fcn = (data[1] >> 1) & 63;`

Backward-incompatible wire format change — all dependent tests need update.
